title: Etaleness of a map of square-zero extensions from its kernel comparison
statement: Let $A^+,A,B^+,B$ be commutative unital rings, $p:A^+\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $q:B^+\twoheadrightarrow B$ surjective ring homomorphisms, and $u^+:A^+\to B^+$, $u:A\to B$ unital ring homomorphisms satisfying $q\circ u^+=u\circ p$. Put $I=\ker p$ and $J=\ker q$, and assume $I^2=0$ and $J^2=0$. Give $I$ its quotient $A$-module structure and $J$ its quotient $B$-module structure. Suppose $u$ is etale, meaning that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-etale-morphism], and that the canonical $B$-linear map $I\otimes_A B\to J$, $i\otimes b\mapsto u^+(i)\widetilde b$, is an isomorphism; here $\widetilde b$ is any lift of $b$ to $B^+$, and $J^2=0$ makes the formula independent of the lift. Then $u^+$ is etale, meaning that $\operatorname{Spec}B^+\to\operatorname{Spec}A^+$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 05YT (lemma-lift-etale-infinitesimal), full statement; the equality of kernels in the diagram means the canonical tensor comparison is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Identify $A^+/I$ with $A$ by the isomorphism $[a]\mapsto p(a)$; its inverse sends $a$ to the class of any lift, independently of that lift. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], $B$ is an etale finitely presented $A$-algebra. Apply [lem-exc-etale-algebra-lift] to $A^+$ and $I$. Obtain an etale $A^+$-algebra $C$, with structural map $v:A^+\to C$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $e:C/IC\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. Write $r:C\twoheadrightarrow B$ for $e$ after quotient; thus $\ker r=IC$ and $rv=up$. The affine etale criterion also gives that $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A^+$ is etale.

The same affine etale criterion gives $H_1(L_{C/A^+})=0$ and $\Omega_{C/A^+}=0$. The zero module is projective: every map out of it lifts uniquely across any surjection. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] applies to $C$, the $A^+$-algebra $B^+$ via $u^+$, and its square-zero ideal $J$. Identify $B^+/J$ with $B$ by $[b^+]\mapsto q(b^+)$. The map $r$ is $A^+$-linear because $rv=up=qu^+$. Lifting $r$ gives an $A^+$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:C\to B^+$ with $q\varphi=r$ and $\varphi v=u^+$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], $C$ is flat over $A^+$. Products of generators show $(IC)^2=I^2C=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-cotangent-flat-base-change-ring] to $A^+\to C$ and $I$: since both ideal squares vanish, multiplication identifies $I\otimes_{A^+}C$ with $IC$. There is a canonical isomorphism $I\otimes_{A^+}C\simeq I\otimes_A B$, sending $i\otimes c$ to $i\otimes r(c)$. Explicitly, its inverse sends $i\otimes b$ to $i\otimes c$ for any $r(c)=b$. If the lift changes by $\sum v(i_k)c_k$ with $i_k\in I$, the difference is $\sum (i_ki)\otimes c_k=0$ since $I^2=0$. Balancing over $A$ follows by lifting $a\in A$ to $a^+\in A^+$ and using the tensor relation $(a^+i)\otimes c=i\otimes v(a^+)c$; another lift acts identically on $I$. The two formulas are inverse on pure tensors, which generate the tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. We obtain an isomorphism $\theta:I\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}IC$, $i\otimes b\mapsto v(i)c$ for any $r(c)=b$.

source.place: Tag 05YT (lemma-lift-etale-infinitesimal), third sentence; Tag 0473 (morphisms-lemma-conormal-functorial-flat), affine proof

proof.text: Let $\beta:I\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ be the assumed comparison. For $i\in I$ and $r(c)=b$, the equations of step 2 give $\varphi(\theta(i\otimes b))=\varphi(v(i)c)=u^+(i)\varphi(c)=\beta(i\otimes b)$, because $q(\varphi(c))=b$. Here $u^+(i)\in J$ since $qu^+(i)=up(i)=0$, and changing the lift of $b$ changes the product by an element of $J^2=0$. Also $q\varphi(IC)=r(IC)=0$, so $\varphi$ restricts to a map $IC\to J$. Equality on pure tensors, followed by additivity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], shows that this restriction composed with $\theta$ is exactly $\beta$. Consequently $\varphi|_{IC}:IC\to J$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05YT (lemma-lift-etale-infinitesimal), final sentence: compatibility of the kernel comparison

proof.text: If $\varphi(c)=0$, then $r(c)=q\varphi(c)=0$, hence $c\in IC$; injectivity of $\varphi|_{IC}$ gives $c=0$. For $b^+\in B^+$ choose $c\in C$ with $r(c)=q(b^+)$. Then $b^+-\varphi(c)\in J$; surjectivity of $\varphi|_{IC}$ supplies $k\in IC$ with $\varphi(k)=b^+-\varphi(c)$, so $\varphi(c+k)=b^+$. Thus $\varphi$ is a bijective $A^+$-algebra homomorphism. Its inverse preserves addition, multiplication, the unit and the $A^+$-structure by applying the injective map $\varphi$ to each required equality. It therefore identifies the map $u^+$ with the etale structure map $v:A^+\to C$ of step 1. Substitution along this $A^+$-algebra isomorphism gives etaleness of $u^+$, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] gives precisely the asserted etaleness of its spectrum.
